Welcome
At Priory Rise, children are at the very centre of everything that we do - aspiring to provide the very best for every child. Children are inspired to learn and develop a genuine love of learning. Relationships are nurturing, warm and supportive and there is a real sense of fun, love and laughter, at every level, which pervades the whole school. Behaviour is exemplary and children are actively encouraged to demonstrate the greatest of courtesy in their interactions with others. Corinne Benham-Smith | Headteacher

PE & Sports Premium
At Priory Rise, we are highly committed to ensuring quality PE and Sports provision for all children. We also believe passionately in the important contribution this aspect of the curriculum makes towards personal development and healthy lifestyles. Since our school opened in 2008, we have therefore given appropriate emphasis to this aspect of our provision.
From September 2013, schools have received additional funding to help them improve the breadth and quality of PE in schools and to increase the levels of participation in sporting activities out of school.
Our additional funding for PE and sports for the last academic year was £10, 865. This has enabled our school to increase the quality and breadth of activities on offer to children and over the past year many more children have participated in a wide range of extra-curricular activities. We have also continued to improve the % of children achieving swimming expectations by the end of Year 6.
We have also paid for membership of the Milton Keynes Primary Sports Partnership. This membership brings several important benefits to the school and the children at Priory Rise. In short, the key benefits of this membership are as follows.
During the academic year 2024-2025 funding for PE and sports will be £21,400.

Admissions
The designated area for Priory Rise School is Tattenhoe Park and South Kingsmead: however we have two ‘secondary’ defined areas – North Kingsmead and Tattenhoe. Children are admitted in September in the academic year that they are 5.
Children are also admitted to other year groups throughout the year if there are places available.
The Local Authority School Admissions Team co-ordinate all school admissions. They process all applications and will contact you to let you know if a place has been allocated.
For children starting school for the first time in September, you can apply online on the council’s website.
Please click here for a guide on applying for a primary school place in Milton Keynes.
To view our Admissions Policy please click here.
Priory Rise School manage the appeal process. For further information and an appeal pack please email office@pr5d.com
Foundation Stage
During the summer term we hold a meeting for all new parents to discuss the school routine and the entry arrangements for our Foundation children. All children starting school in September will have an opportunity to spend some time in their new class with their teacher and will also receive a home visit in the autumn term from their class teacher prior to starting school.
Foundation Stage teachers also make visits to local pre-schools in the summer term before the children begin at school. Home visits take place during the first week of the autumn term, as our Foundation aged children have a staggered start and do not start full days until the middle of September.

Early Birds and Night Owls
Our Breakfast Club (Early Birds) and After School Club (Night Owls) is run by staff of Priory Rise School. We believe that Early Birds and Night Owls should have the same ethos as the rest of the school, ensuring the best provision and consistency for your children. Our playworker team work closely with families and children to ensure that we provide a programme of play and social education activities that meet the individual needs of the children in their care. We welcome full-time Reception classes to Year 6 children.
Aims of the Clubs:
Help improve pupils’ attendance and punctuality.
Improve social interaction skills between pupils.

Timings
The gates on Priestley Drive will be opened at 7:30am each morning. After this time, children will be able to arrive at Early Birds breakfast club.
From 8:30am onwards the children in Foundation and Key Stage 1 will be escorted to their classes. The children in Key Stage 2 will walk to their allocated collection points within school.
For Night Owls, Reception children will be collected by a member of staff from their classrooms at 3:00pm, as will Year 1 & Year 2 children from 3:10pm. Staff will register your child’s attendance on arrival. KS2 children will walk to the small hall from 3:20pm onwards. Night Owls runs from 3:00pm until 6:00pm. Please note there is a late collection fee if your child is not picked up promptly.
If any children have enrolled in an after-school club, they will be escorted by the club leader to Night Owls when the club finishes at 4:15pm.
Staffing
Early Birds and Night Owls are staffed by employees of the school who either have an additional role in school during the day or who are specifically employed to cover the clubs. This allows a seamless transition from school expectations to club expectations.
Our team is professional, enthusiastic and offer high quality, affordable childcare, in a caring and nurturing environment, which encompasses from Early Years Reception through to Year 6. This gives the children and staff the best opportunity to build up strong, trusting, and have meaningful relationships with each other.
All our staff have undertaken the pre-employment checks required as detailed in the document, Keeping Children Safe in Education, hold a valid First Aid certification, in addition to a Food Hygiene certification.

Personal, Social & Health Education
At Priory Rise we place huge importance on providing our children with the knowledge and skills they will need to be successful not only in the next stage of their learning journey but as they become young adults in the world in which they live. We want children to develop a positive self image, feeling free to be unique - an individual - and develop the confidence to challenge negativity, inequality, and prejudice. We want our young people to know how to keep themselves healthy and safe, now and in the future. Our Personal, Social and Health education (PSHE) provides children with lots of opportunities and experiences to manage emotions, and develop communication skills and strategies, in order to live in a culturally diverse world, celebrate differences and maintain positive relationships.
We use Jigsaw as a basis for teaching and learning which will equip children with essential life skills. This important work starts in the Nursery with weekly activities/lessons building on knowledge and fine-tuning skills in children as they move through the school to Year 6. Six themes, lasting a half term, are followed each year, these are:
Our monthly values link very closely to these lessons/activities, as children learn to apply these to their behaviours in their everyday lives.
In addition, we teach our children Restorative Practices, where they learn to make meaningful connections with others, learning to behave positively, even when this is challenging; as this is what we believe makes the difference for a positive world. Adults model to children, in every interaction, how what they have to say and their feelings are valued, so children learn how to talk through difficult situations to find resolution. Children come to understand there may be more than one way to successfully problem-solve, learning to develop empathy and understanding for others.

About our Nursery
Our nursery is a key part of Priory Rise School, facilitated by an experienced team who work very closely together and with the rest of the staff across the Foundation Stage. Nursery is currently staffed by a full-time teacher, 3 nursery nurses and a teaching assistant. We offer a warm and welcoming nursery environment which provides well-resourced inside and outside areas. Your child will be able to extend their learning by exploring and playing with resources designed to capture and develop their interests. Learning will be developed through the characteristics of effective learning and the 7 areas of the early years foundation stage (EYFS).
Your child’s learning and progress will be captured in Tapestry (an online learning journal), something which has been highly successful and popular with parents. We recognise that each child is unique and progresses at their own rate in their own way. Our caring and nurturing staff will enable your child to develop to be the best version of themselves by providing individualised learning through observation, questioning, exploration and building on children’s interests. Nursery children will visit other parts of the school; the small hall to do P.E. once a week and the library to borrow a book, enabling the children to become familiar with the larger school community around them.
The EYFS framework was given a significant review and new guidance became statutory in September 2021. More information about the framework can be found by clicking the below link.
